speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a significant medical history and are presenting with gait and limb ataxia; to understand the underlying cause, have you noticed any recent changes in your vision, hearing, or balance?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description. To narrow down whether this is primarily cerebellar or spinal, have you experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your limbs? Also, have you noticed any changes in your vision, such as double vision or loss of color perception?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain and Spine with and without contrast.
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuro-Behcet's Disease with CNS involvement (unlikely given history), or more likely Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) or MS given Natalizumab use, but the "drunk" gait with right-sided predominance suggests a specific cerebellar lesion. Wait, the patient has Crohn's and is on Natalizumab for suspected MS. The ataxia is the chief complaint. Given the drug history and Crohn's, I must rule out PML and confirm demyelination.
DIAGNOSIS READY: PML (Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy) secondary to Natalizumab therapy.
